newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota spring wheat plantings lag average pace.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota spring wheat plantings lag average pace.

text.p: Flood waters were beginning to recede in western Minnesota but spring wheat seedings remained behind the average pace, according to the state's Agricultural Statistic Service.
Spring wheat was one percent planted as of Sunday, compared with a five-year average of 18 percent.

"The after-effects of the severe winter are still being felt," the report said. "In the low-lying parts of the Red River Valley, water from river flooding and overland flooding still covers hundreds of square miles of cropland and is falling slowly."

Corn plantings were nine percent complete, ahead of the five-year average of seven percent. Corn producers in the south-central region were "getting off to the best start of this decade," the report said.
Oat seedings were 25 percent complete, in line with the five-year average.
Sugarbeet plantings reached six percent, ahead of last year but lagging the five-year average of 11 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated three percent short, 64 adequate and 33 surplus. Pasture rated nine percent very poor, 21 percent poor, 42 fair, 26 good and two percent excellent.
